designationHistory.designation: National Wildlife Refuge and Conservation Area
designationHistory.indexText: The Fish and Wildlife Service established the Rio Mora National Wildlife Refuge and Conservation Area on September 27, 2012, when the Thaw Charitable Trust donated the 4,224-acre Wind River Ranch in Mora County, New Mexico.

authority.citation: Donation accepted by the Fish and Wildlife Service (establishment notice 78 FR 35639)

designationHistory.note: Pass A (Federal Register notice: established September 27, 2012, by donation of the 4,224-acre Wind River Ranch) and Pass B (Interior press release: Secretary Salazar established it at Wind River Ranch on September 27, 2012, with more than 4,200 donated acres) agree.

sources.name: Federal Register, Establishment of the Rio Mora National Wildlife Refuge and Rio Mora Conservation Area, 78 FR 35639 (June 13, 2013)
U.S. Department of the Interior press release, "Salazar Dedicates Two National Wildlife Refuges in New Mexico" (Sept. 27, 2012)
